For providers that still emit unflagged usage (excluding Ollama, LM Studio, declared compatible pairs, Anthropic's conservatively checked four categories, Gemini's bounded accounting mapping and the shared OpenAI/xAI Responses mapping), explicit all-zero usage is still indistinguishable from absent metadata and partial-positive metadata may still be treated as provider totals. title: Use another agent CLI as the inference backend
contract: The copilot-acp provider drives GitHub Copilot CLI as an external Agent Client Protocol subprocess and presents it to Hermes as an OpenAI-compatible client; provider projection folds an agent-shaped provider's own completed tool work back into Hermes's transcript so Hermes never re-runs finished work. Inventory: providers.copilot-acp, providers.copilot-acp-client, providers.provider-projection.
governance: Structurally unmediatable as a provider: the privileged effects occur inside the subprocess before any Nerva code sees them.
historical_exclusion_reason: Provider projection is the giveaway: this imports another agent's completed tool work into the transcript, which means another agent ran tools on this machine and Nerva records the result rather than authorising the act. Every effect that subprocess performs — files, shell, network — bypasses the Action Kernel, the approval queue and the audit log by construction, and no wrapper can retrofit mediation onto work that already happened. Adopting it would hollow out the exact property that distinguishes Nerva. Re-open path: none as a provider; if the owner wants another agent's help, it belongs on the MCP/subagent path where its tool calls are individually mediated.
